headlines.title: Questions linger about lead pollution from Iowa blast, despite officials’ assurances
headlines.description: Scientists and Iowa residents said questions remain about how much contamination the Army’s detonation of lead azide caused, though they were hopeful about the initial results.

headlines.title: Army detonates cache of lead explosives, with toxic plume possible across Iowa
headlines.description: The Army detonated a stockpile of unstable lead azide explosives in Iowa on Wednesday morning. A toxic dust plume could travel for miles.

headlines.title: ‘Shocking’ decline seen in hep B vaccination against incurable virus, including babies with infected mothers
headlines.description: Fewer newborns are being vaccinated against hepatitis B, an incurable infection that can lead to liver disease, a large new analysis has found.

headlines.title: Too young to be vaccinated for measles? Babies face growing threats from outbreaks
headlines.description: As measles outbreaks continue to soar, a new question has emerged: Should doctors give measles shots earlier to better protect babies?

headlines.title: Thanksgiving food safety best practices
headlines.description: Sometimes preparing Thanksgiving food can pose health risks as harmful bacteria can potentially grow and thrive if food is not cooked thoroughly. And at large gatherings, storing food at the right temperature can be challenging. Rutgers University Food Microbiology Professor Donald Schaffner spoke with NBC News’ Ellison Barber about implementing safe kitchen practices to help stop the spread of food borne illnesses.

headlines.title: Small-town rural pharmacies in jeopardy over prescription drug costs and reimbursements
headlines.description: NBC News' Priscilla Thompson reports for the series “The Cost of Denial” about the squeeze rural pharmacies are feeling, often being reimbursed less for prescription drugs than they pay. Some blame pharmacy benefit managers, or “PBMs”, the powerful middlemen that negotiate drug prices with manufacturers and help determine how much those pharmacies are reimbursed.

headlines.title: Army says controlled detonation of lead explosives was ‘a huge success’
headlines.description: After the Army detonated a cache of toxic explosives in Iowa, the Environmental Protection Agency said there is zero detection of airborne lead near the detonation site. NBC News' Shaquille Brewster and Dr. Juanita Mora of the American Lung Association discuss the cleanup plans and safety tips.

headlines.title: Former St. Jude Patient Returns to Aid Next Generation
headlines.description: For three years, radiology technologist Ted VanAusdall has performed CT scans and provided smiles at St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital. But long before he was treating young patients, he was one of them. NBC’s Savannah Sellers reports for TODAY on his cancer journey before he found his way back to help others. Then, Marlo Thomas, the hospital’s national outreach director, shares insights into St. Jude’s life studies.
